title: Subtracting constants preserves degree
statement: Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ have Fourier degree at most $k$, where $n,k\in\mathbb N$, and let $c\in\mathbb R$. Then the function $x\mapsto f(x)-c$ has Fourier degree at most $k$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function of arity $n$
replaced: Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$ have Fourier degree at most $k\in\mathbb N$, and let $c\in\bbr$. The function $x\mapsto f(x)-c$ also has Fourier degree at most $k$.
